claim: Corollary 4.21 (p. 139) is Uçar's central determinacy theorem: for a closed orbisurface O of constant curvature kappa in R with M dihedral points of orders 2m_1,...,2m_M and N cone points of orders n_1,...,n_N, if kappa != 0 then 'kappa together with the spectrum' determines M+2N and the multiset {m_1,...,m_M,n_1,n_1,...,n_N,n_N} (part iii), and if additionally the mirror locus is trivial, determines the number of cone points and the multiset of their orders alone (part iv).
stance_target: What Uçar's thesis proves about determining the cone-order multiset of an orientable constant-curvature orbisurface
scope_conditions: Closed orbisurface, constant curvature kappa != 0
quoted_support: If kappa != 0, then kappa together with the spectrum determines the number M+2N as well as the multiset {m1,...,mM,n1,n1,n2,n2,...,nN,nN}. ... If the mirror locus is trivial and kappa != 0, then kappa together with the spectrum determines the number of cone points as well as the multiset of all orders {n1,...,nN}.

claim: Corollary 4.23 (p. 140) specializes Corollary 4.21(iv) to ORIENTABLE orbisurfaces: for O closed orientable with constant curvature kappa != 0, kappa together with the spectrum determines the Euler characteristic of O and of the underlying space X_O; this generalizes Dryden-Strohmaier's [DS09, Prop. 3.3] result which was previously known only for kappa=-1.

scope_conditions: Closed orientable orbisurface, constant curvature kappa != 0

Then kappa together with the spectrum of O determines the Euler characteristic of O as well as the Euler characteristic of the underlying space XO. ... this fact was previously known in the special case of closed orientable orbisurfaces of constant curvature kappa = -1 (see [DS09, Proposition 3.3]).

claim: Orientability is used essentially: because an orientable orbisurface has a trivial mirror locus and all its singular points are cone points, Corollary 4.21(iv) applies directly; Corollary 4.23's proof states this explicitly.
stance_target: Hypotheses of Uçar's orientable-orbisurface determinacy result
scope_conditions: Proof of Corollary 4.23
quoted_support: Furthermore, since the orbisurface O is orientable, its mirror locus is trivial and all singular points are cone points. Thus, by Corollary 4.21 (iv), we can deduce from the spectrum the total number of all cone points as well as the multiset of all their orders.

claim: Corollaries 4.24 (p.140-141) and 4.25 (p.141) give finer determinacy within restricted subclasses: orbifolds with no cone points or no dihedral points (Cor. 4.24), and orbifolds where every dihedral point has a unique order among dihedral points and every cone point has a unique order among cone points (Cor. 4.25) -- in both restricted classes the spectrum determines the full singular set with orders, still via the full spectrum, not a finite coefficient count.
stance_target: Scope of Uçar's finer determinacy results

Then within A1, the spectrum again determines chi(O), chi(XO), the length of the mirror locus, the number of dihedral points with their order, and the number of cone points with their orders.
